The name Insijam carries the meaning “Victorious and Victorious” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. historical_references.reference: Insijam was the name of a fortress and small town on the outskirts of Baghdad during the Abbasid Caliphate. It was famous for its strategically important position on the Tigris River and its role in the defense of Baghdad against various invaders. The name Insijam is believed to derive from the Arabic words 'as-sijam', meaning 'the brushwood', referring to the dense thicket of reeds and brush along the river bank.

Insijam is also mentioned in the works of Persian poet and scholar Omar Khayyam as a place of pilgrimage for the followers of the Sufi saint Shams-i Tabriz. According to the tales, Shams-i Tabriz would often retreat to Insijam to meditate and seek enlightenment, making it a site of spiritual significance for Sufis.
